newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia sees IMF deal in few months - official.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia sees IMF deal in few months - official.

text.p: Yugoslavia expects to conclude a deal with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and other financial organisations within months, a Yugoslav Chamber official said on Wednesday.
"All government reports indicate the deal with the IMF will be reached in three to four months," Mira Lukic, secretary to the Chamber's board for economic cooperation with the world told Reuters.
"This is one of the main prerequisites for reaching the economic policy targets set for 1997," she said.
The crippling U.N. sanctions imposed on Yugoslavia in May 1992 isolated the country from the international community and banned its access to world's financial markets and organisations.

The measures were lifted last October, but the so called outer wall of sanctions remained in place preventing country's return to the IMF and the World Bank and thus its access to foreign funds urgently needed for revival of the economy.

Belgrade's return to the international community was conditional upon its cooperation with the Hague crime tribunal for Bosnia and respect of human rights especially in its Kosovo province which has a majority Albanian population.
